strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_ask_diary:
The diary — yes, I have it. Isabelle lent it to me years ago. The visions in it correspond to genuine stellar events; quite remarkable.
I won't simply hand it over, however. Knowledge requires reciprocity.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_ask_isabe:
Isabelle. Untethered, which is my professional assessment.
I have her diary — she lent it to me for research. Her visions are extraordinarily accurate by stellar standards.
I've been meaning to return it, but I've needed my equipment first.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_ask_resea:
The temporal distortions in this house correspond directly to planetary alignments — I've charted over three hundred correlations.
But my equipment has been scattered and I can't complete the work.
Which, incidentally, also prevents me from returning something I owe Isabelle.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_complete:
The diary is with Isabelle now, which is correct.
I can see {keys_collected|round} of the 4 celestial alignments forming already — the curse is weakening.
Find whoever holds the remaining {flag:keys_remaining|round} {flag:keys_remaining|plural:key/keys}.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_first_1:
Greetings, earthbound traveler! I am [b]Professor Orion Starweaver[/b] — astronomer, celestial cartographer, and currently the only person in this house paying attention to the sky.
Which, given that the sky holds all the answers, is frankly embarrassing for everyone else.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_first_2: Yes? I'm rather busy. The upper atmosphere isn't going to chart itself.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_first_2.c: I'm looking for a diary — from the Dreamer.
What are you studying up here?
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_has_both_:
Both! Telescope AND star chart — you are extraordinarily capable for someone who isn't an astronomer.
With these I can resume my observations of the temporal distortions in the upper atmosphere.
The patterns have been quite clear, once you know how to read them.

The diary — there. A fair exchange between professionals.
Return it to Isabelle. She is in the west wing and she has been untethered without it.
The visions in those pages are genuine, incidentally. The stars confirmed several of them.

Obtained Personal Diary
Take it to Isabelle — west wing.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_has_chart:
The star chart — superb. {item_count:item=Star Chart|round} of 2 items, after a fashion.
Still need the telescope. Ground floor study, I believe.
Bring it up here and we have a deal.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_has_teles:
Excellent — the telescope! {item_count:item=Telescope|round} of 2 items collected.
Still need the star chart from the locked box downstairs.
Combination is on a stone plaque in the garden. The Gardener will point you to it.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_needs_bot:
Still need both items — telescope and star chart.
You have {item_count:item=Telescope|bool:the telescope/no telescope} and {item_count:item=Star Chart|bool:the star chart/no star chart}.
Telescope: ground floor study. Star chart: locked box downstairs, combination on a stone plaque in the garden.
strings.dialogue.astronomer.astronomer_the_deal:
I need two things. My telescope — it was in the study on the ground floor when I last saw it.
And my star chart, which I locked in a box downstairs. The three-digit combination is engraved on a stone plaque in the garden.
The Gardener will know where the plaque is.
Both items. Then the diary is yours.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_ask_family:
The Ashfields. The whole family — they were all coming for Christmas in 1943.
I had everything planned. Then the house... changed.
I've kept cooking. I thought if I stayed ready, eventually they'd come back.
[i]a quiet pause[/i]
Well. Perhaps now they will.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_ask_help:
Oh, bless you. Yes.
The pantry needs to be open first — talk to Cornelius in the workshop if it isn't already.
Once it's open, I need three things.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_ask_pantry:
The latch jammed years ago and I've never been strong enough to force it.
I asked Cornelius — the Inventor in the workshop — to fix it but he lost his tools.
If you've already helped him, it should be open now. If not, he's in the workshop.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_complete:
The kitchen smells right again.
I always thought if I kept cooking, eventually the family would come back.
Maybe after all this, they will.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_first_1:
Oh, come in, come in — mind the step, it's always been uneven.
I'm [b]Margaret[/b]. I've been cooking in this kitchen for longer than makes sense now.
I was meant to be making the Christmas feast. The family was coming.
I've been keeping everything ready, just in case.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_first_2:
A proper feast loaf — that's what this kitchen needs. Not just bread.
But the pantry's been stuck for years and I can't get to the flour.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_first_2.choice3: Can I help you get what you need?
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_has_all_1:
Flour, honey, herbs — oh my goodness, all three.
[i]she clasps her hands[/i]
This is everything I need.
Now step back and let me work.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_has_all_2:
There. The feast loaf — smell that.
I found this [color=#3f8f4f]Crystal Key[/color] tucked inside the recipe box years ago. I've been keeping it safe the way you keep anything precious.
Take it. The green pedestal in the main hall — that's where it belongs.
Go on now. The others are waiting.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_has_all_3:
Obtained Green Crystal Key
You now have {keys_collected|round} of 4 Crystal Keys.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_ingredients_ask:
Flour — in the pantry, once Cornelius fixes the door.
Honey — in the larder, just through that door there.
Dried herbs — hanging above the stove, been there for years.
Bring me all three and I can bake something worth giving.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_needs_ingredients:
Three ingredients — I need all of them before I can start.
Flour: {item_count:item=Flour Sack|bool:got it/pantry, now open}.
Honey: {item_count:item=Jar of Honey|bool:got it/larder, through that door}.
Herbs: {item_count:item=Dried Herbs|bool:got it/hanging above the stove}.
strings.dialogue.cook.cook_waiting_for_pantry:
Cornelius in the workshop — he can fix the pantry door once he has his toolbox.
Once it's open: flour's in the pantry, honey's in the larder, herbs above the stove.
Bring me all three.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_0keys_ask_cor:
I'm not sure I have survived, exactly.
I exist. I observe. I think.
For the first twenty years I was quite despairing. After that I became... determined.
Determination is surprisingly sustaining.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_0keys_ask_cur:
The ritual Theodore used was a binding — it tied the house and everyone inside it to a fixed moment.
The Crystal Keys were hidden inside it as release mechanisms. Theodore built them in deliberately, I think — some part of him knew he might need a way out.
Or perhaps he was just careful, once, in his life.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_0keys_ask_hin:
Edmund in the library is a good first stop — he's methodical and he'll explain things clearly.
He's been working on understanding the curse for decades. What he knows, you should know too.
Through the east corridor, up the main stairs.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_1key_ask_keys:
Each key resonates with something the holder represents — knowledge, dreams, creation, protection.
When all four are placed in the pedestals, those four forces together are enough to break the binding Theodore created.
He balanced the curse on four pillars. We remove them together.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_1key_ask_them:
Better than I feared, honestly.
Edmund is still working. Isabelle still dreams, even if it frightens her. Margaret still cooks.
Cedric has maintained his post without relief for eighty years and has not once complained about it.
They are more resilient than I gave them credit for.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_1key_ask_who:
Each of them needs something lost returned to them.
Isabelle has been losing herself without her diary — she's in the west wing.
Margaret is waiting on ingredients she can't reach — kitchen.
Cedric is maintaining his post regardless — east vault.
Any of them will do. Follow what calls to you.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_2keys_ask_out:
Very little, I'm afraid.
Occasionally someone comes near the house — we can sense it — but no one has entered until you.
I assume the war ended. I assume the world continued.
I try to hold onto the assumption that it got better.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_2keys_ask_the:
Theodore faded a long time ago.
He tried to undo what he'd done almost immediately — it broke him, I think, realising what he'd caused.
He became less and less present over the years. By 1970 he was gone entirely.
He never stopped being sorry. I suppose that's something.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_2keys_ask_who:
Two more keys still outstanding.
Check who you haven't yet helped — Edmund, Isabelle, Margaret, Cedric.
Whichever two you haven't visited, start there. They've been waiting a long time.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_3keys_ask_aft:
I've thought about this for a long time.
I believe we rest. Properly, finally.
What that means exactly — I don't know. But I know it's better than this.
[i]quietly[/i]
I'm not afraid of it.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_3keys_ask_las:
Look at who you haven't helped yet — Edmund, Isabelle, Margaret, Cedric.
One of them is still waiting.
They've kept that key safe for eighty years. Whatever they need from you, it matters to them.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_3keys_ask_rea:
I have been ready for a very long time.
Go. Find the last key. Come back to the pedestals.
I'll be here.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_ask_others_in:
There were eight of us when the curse took hold.
Four remain who can still help you — Edmund in the library, Isabelle in the west wing, Margaret in the kitchen, Cedric guarding the vault.
The others have... faded. Become part of the house.
I try not to think about that too often.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_ask_theodore_:
He was afraid.
The war was coming — he could feel it even out here. He thought the house would be destroyed, that everyone he loved would be taken.
He found an old ritual in the library and he used it without fully understanding it.
He thought he was being protective.
[i]a pause[/i]
He was [b]twenty-three years old[/b].
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_ask_whatnow:
That's the right question. And I'm grateful you're asking it rather than simply running.
Most people, I imagine, would run.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_complete_choi:
The exit portal is open — through the main hall.
Go. Be free.
We will be alright now.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_complete_scho:
All four pedestals lit.
[i]she pauses, and then almost to herself[/i]
Edmund trusted you enough to give you that key without his book.
He hasn't trusted anyone with anything since 1943.
[i]she looks at you properly[/i]
Thank you. For all of it.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_complete_stan:
All four pedestals.
After [b]eighty years[/b].
[i]she is quiet for a long moment[/i]
[wave]Thank you, Elena.[/wave] For doing what I spent my whole life trying to do.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_end_ask_free:
I believe so.
I've held onto that belief for [b]eighty years[/b] — it's what kept me from fading the way the others did.
I think I'll finally find out if I was right.
[i]a small smile[/i]
[color=#c9a24b]I rather think I was.[/color]
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_end_ask_theod:
I forgave him a long time ago.
He was frightened and he loved us all in his clumsy way.
The hard part wasn't forgiving Theodore.
The hard part was forgiving myself for not stopping him.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_end_goodbye:
Goodbye, Elena.
Thank you for coming in.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_end_portal:
The portal is in the main hall.
Go home.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_intro_1:
Oh — you're real. You're actually here.
I've been waiting so long I stopped being certain what was real.
I am [b]Cordelia Ashfield[/b]. This is — was — my family's house.
Please, stay a moment. I have to explain something important.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_intro_2:
My great-nephew [b]Theodore[/b] performed a ritual in [b]1943[/b].
He was trying to preserve this house and everyone in it — make it last forever.
It worked. In the worst possible way.
We have been here ever since. The house is intact. We are intact.
[color=#8b2f2f]But we cannot leave. We cannot age. We cannot rest.[/color]
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_intro_curse:
I have spent [b]eighty years[/b] trying to understand what he did well enough to undo it.
And I believe I finally have.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_intro_curse.c: What do you need me to do?
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_intro_solutio:
[b]Four Crystal Keys[/b]. [b]Four pedestals[/b] in the main hall.
When all four are activated together, the curse breaks.
Each key is held by one of the people still trapped here — and each of them needs something from you before they'll part with it.
Edmund is in the library. His key is [color=#8b2f2f]red[/color].
Isabelle is in the west wing. Her key is [color=#c9a24b]yellow[/color].
Margaret is in the kitchen. Her key is [color=#3f8f4f]green[/color].
Cedric guards the vault. His key is [color=#2f5f8b]blue[/color].
Find them. Help them. Bring the keys to the pedestals.
I will be here.
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_progress_0key:
You have {keys_collected} of the four keys.
There's no rush — but there is urgency, if that distinction makes sense.
Tell me more about the curse.
How have you survived eighty years of this?
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_progress_1key:
{keys_collected} of four — you've made a start.
Three more people in this house still need your help.
Who should I go to next?
What do the Crystal Keys actually do?
How are the others holding up?
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_progress_2key:
Halfway there — {keys_collected} of four.
You're doing what I tried to do for decades and couldn't.
I never had the freedom to move between them properly. You do.
What's happened outside, do you know?
strings.dialogue.cordelia.cordelia_progress_3key:
{keys_collected} of four. One more.
I can feel the binding loosening — even from here, I can feel it.
Someone in this house still has the last key.
What happens to everyone after the curse breaks?
I'm almost done. Are you ready?
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_ask_diary:
My diary. I had it once — I wrote everything in it.
I gave it to Professor Starweaver to study, and then...
No, wait. That's not right. I can't remember the order of things.
There was a letter somewhere. I keep feeling the letter.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_ask_diary_now:
The observatory. Professor Starweaver — upstairs, east corridor.
He'll want his telescope back, and there's something else he lost.
A star chart. He mentioned it was locked in a box downstairs. The combination is somewhere in the garden.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_ask_key:
The yellow key. Yes. It's here somewhere — I've dreamed it clearly.
But I can't reach it yet. I need to remember something first.
There was a letter. Somewhere in this house. If I could just see it...
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_ask_visions:
I dream around things more than through them now.
I used to write everything down — every vision, every fragment.
But my diary is gone and without it I can't find the edges of myself.
I keep feeling like something was written for me, somewhere in this house. A letter, maybe.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_ask_who_wrote:
I'm not sure I should say.
Something I've been holding onto for a very long time.
It doesn't matter now — what matters is the diary.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_complete:
I dreamed this moment clearly, for once.
Go. The four pedestals.
I'll still be here dreaming — but perhaps after this, the dreams will finally be peaceful.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_first_1:
Oh... someone is here.
I thought I dreamed you, but you're still here when I blink.
I am — I was — I think I am still [b]Isabelle[/b].
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_first_2:
There is something in this room I can't quite reach. A key, I think. Warm like afternoon light.
But I can't... the edges of things keep moving.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_first_2.choice3: I'm looking for a Crystal Key.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_has_diary_1:
My diary.
[i]she holds it without opening it[/i]
I don't need to read it. I just needed to know it existed.
That I existed. That I wrote things down and they were real.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_has_diary_2:
The yellow key — I dreamed someone would come for it. I dreamed you, I think.
Take it to the yellow pedestal in the main hall.
All four together — that's how it ends.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_has_diary_3:
Obtained Yellow Crystal Key
You now have {keys_collected|round} of 4 Crystal Keys.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_has_letter_1:
Oh.
[i]she takes it, very slowly[/i]
Oh, I know this handwriting.
[i]she reads in silence for a moment[/i]
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_letter_hint:
A letter. Somewhere in the house — written for me, I think.
I can feel it the way you feel a word you can't quite say.
Find it. Bring it here.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_needs_diary:
The diary is with Professor Starweaver. The observatory — upstairs, east corridor.
He'll want his telescope back, and a star chart he locked away.
The combination for the box is in the garden.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_needs_letter:
A letter. Somewhere in the house.
I can feel it the way you feel a word you can't quite say.
Find it — bring it here.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_remembers:
I remember now. The diary — I gave it to Professor Starweaver.
He's in the observatory. Upstairs, east corridor.
He'll want something in return. He always does.
strings.dialogue.dreamer.dreamer_remembers.choic: Do you remember where your diary is?
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_ask_cabinet:
Yes, I have it. Edmund gave it to me once — a long time ago now.
I still do.
But the garden has been missing something. Perhaps we can help each other.
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_ask_garden:
It used to be full of roses along the east wall. Three of them in particular — deep red, always in bloom.
When the curse came, they went into the display case as if to preserve themselves.
I've missed them terribly. But you were asking about something else?
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_ask_scholar:
Edmund sent you?
[i]a small quiet pause[/i]
He still thinks of the key, then.
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_complete:
The roses are back where they belong.
Help Edmund find what he's looking for.
He always worked so hard. He deserved better than all this.
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_first_1:
Oh, a visitor. How lovely.
Welcome to my garden — though I suppose it's been autumn here for some time now.
I am [b]Elara[/b]. I tend to what remains.
Things still grow here, if you encourage them properly.
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_first_2: Is there something I can help you with, dear?
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_first_2.choic: I'm looking for a cabinet key.
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_has_roses_1:
Three roses. Oh, they're perfect.
[i]she cups them gently[/i]
They smell exactly as they should. Some things the curse couldn't touch after all.
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_has_roses_2:
Here — the cabinet key.
Tell Edmund the garden is blooming again.
He used to say that's all anything needed — the right conditions, and a little patience.
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_needs_roses:
You have {item_count:item=Rose|round} of 3 roses so far.
The display case is in the east room — three weighted panels, all pressed at the same time.
Find something heavy for each one and they'll all release together.
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_rose_request:
Three red roses — they're in the old display case in the east room.
The case has three weighted panels. You'll need something heavy on each one at the same time to release the latch.
Have a look around the room for what's there.
Bring all three roses back here and I'll give you the key.
strings.dialogue.gardener.gardener_sent_by_schol:
Edmund sent you?
[i]a small quiet pause[/i]
He still thinks of the key, then.
Three red roses — east room display case. Three weighted panels, all at once to open it.
Bring them here and I'll give you the key.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_ask_curse:
Four keys. Four pedestals. Main hall.
I have known this for some time. I have been waiting for someone capable of retrieving them.
The Blue Crystal Key is inside this vault. I will open it under the correct conditions.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_ask_key:
It is inside. I will open the vault when two conditions are met.
No sooner.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_ask_vault:
The Blue Crystal Key is inside. Also the Ancient Seal of Binding, various confiscated articles, and forty years of accumulated documentation.
Nothing leaves this vault without proper procedure.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_complete:
The vault is secure. The Seal is contained.
For eighty years, I have done what I was posted here to do.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_first_1:
Stand where I can see you.
I am [b]Master Cedric Voss[/b]. Guardian of this vault. Protector of what should not be left unprotected.
State your business.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_first_2.choic: What are you guarding in there?
Do you know how to break the curse?
I need the Blue Crystal Key.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_has_both_1:
Ancient Seal. Merchant's Ledger. Both present and accounted for.
Conditions satisfied. Opening the vault.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_has_both_2:
The Blue Crystal Key.
The Seal is secured. The Ledger is returned. Order has been maintained.
The blue pedestal is in the main hall. That is where the key goes.
All four together will end the curse. That is the correct procedure.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_has_both_3:
Obtained Blue Crystal Key
You now have {keys_collected|round} of 4 Crystal Keys.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_has_ledger_on:
Merchant's Ledger — received. Condition two met.
Still outstanding: Ancient Seal.
East wing, cracked wall. The Inventor's hammer will break through.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_has_seal_only:
Ancient Seal — received. Condition one met.
Still outstanding: Merchant's Ledger.
Iron box on the table behind me. Ornate Key opens it — west rooms.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_needs_both:
Vault status: {item_count:item=Ancient Seal|bool:Seal — received/Seal — outstanding} | {item_count:item=Merchant Ledger|bool:Ledger — received/Ledger — outstanding}.
Both required before the vault opens.
Seal: east wing, cracked wall, Inventor's hammer. Ledger: iron box on the table, Ornate Key from the west rooms.
strings.dialogue.guardian.guardian_the_condition:
Two conditions.
First: the Ancient Seal of Binding must be secured here. I sense it loose in the east wing — behind a cracked wall. The Inventor's hammer will get you through.
Second: the Merchant's Ledger must be returned. It is inside the iron box on the table behind me. The Ornate Key opens it — check the west rooms.
Both items. Then the vault opens.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_ask_cook:
Margaret. Yes. She's been making do without flour for too long.
I'd have fixed the pantry years ago but I can't work without my full kit.
It's a simple latch mechanism — thirty seconds with the right tools.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_ask_help:
Toolbox. Two pieces. That's the whole problem.
Get me the pieces and I can fix the pantry. Fix the pantry and Margaret can bake.
Everything downstream of that sorts itself.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_ask_split:
House shifted about thirty years ago — moved whole rooms around. Toolbox was open on the bench.
Handle ended up in the workshop, body went down to the cellar.
Don't ask me to explain the physics. I've tried.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_complete:
Pantry's open. Flour's in there, honey's in the larder, herbs above the stove.
Take the lot to Margaret.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_first_1:
Workshop's this way — mind the lathe, it lists left.
I'm [b]Cornelius[/b]. Been here since '43, been building since '44.
First year was, admittedly, mostly sitting.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_first_2:
Right — current problem. My toolbox is in two pieces and I can't fix anything without it.
Including the pantry door, which Margaret has been waiting on for years.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_first_2.choic: How did your toolbox end up in pieces?
I heard Margaret needs the pantry door fixed.
What do you need help with?
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_has_toolbox_1:
Both halves — yes.
[i]he snaps the toolbox together[/i]
Thirty seconds, as advertised. Now — the pantry.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_has_toolbox_2:
Pantry door's fixed — latch mechanism reset, should open freely now.
Flour's in there. Honey's in the larder off the kitchen. Dried herbs are above the stove.
Margaret will know what to do with all three.
She's in the kitchen. Probably still waiting.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_has_toolbox_3:
Pantry access unlocked.
Flour Sack, Jar of Honey and Dried Herbs are now accessible.
Take them all to Margaret.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_needs_toolbox:
Two pieces needed — Handle and Body.
Handle: {item_count:item=Toolbox Handle|bool:got it/east bench in this workshop}.
Body: {item_count:item=Toolbox Body|bool:got it/cellar, ground floor}.
Bring both here to the workbench.
strings.dialogue.inventor.inventor_the_task:
Toolbox Handle — east bench, right here in the workshop.
Toolbox Body — cellar, ground floor.
Bring both to the workbench here. I'll have it assembled in thirty seconds.
strings.dialogue.item.ancient_seal_pickup:
A mystical seal carved with protective wards and binding runes.
It pulses with contained power - clearly a [color=#8b2f2f]dangerous artifact[/color] that should be properly secured.
strings.dialogue.item.blue_pedestal_active:
The Blue Pedestal radiates protective power and the weight of guarded secrets.
The Guardian's wisdom flows through the crystal, unlocking the final barrier.
strings.dialogue.item.blue_pedestal_active_2: Protective energy surrounds the house like an ancient shield dissolving.
strings.dialogue.item.blue_pedestal_inactive:
A sapphire pedestal carved with symbols of protection and ancient secrets.
It emanates quiet power, waiting for the Blue Crystal Key to complete the circle.
strings.dialogue.item.cabinet_key_pickup:
A small brass key on a faded ribbon.
Something about the way it was kept suggests it was never meant to be given away - only held onto.
strings.dialogue.item.dried_herbs_pickup:
A tied bundle of dried herbs hanging above the stove - rosemary, thyme, something sharper.
They smell exactly as they should, as though time forgot to touch them.
strings.dialogue.item.entrance_door:
The heavy oak door you entered through stands firmly shut.
The handle turns, but the door refuses to budge - as if the house itself holds it closed.
strings.dialogue.item.entrance_door_2:
Strange symbols have appeared along the door frame, glowing faintly with an otherworldly light.
A whispered voice seems to echo from within the wood:
	[i][shake rate=8 level=1]'None may leave until the four keys sing as one.'[/shake][/i]
strings.dialogue.item.entrance_door_3:
The door remembers your entry, but it has forgotten how to let you leave.
You sense this threshold will not open again until the house's curse is broken.
strings.dialogue.item.feast_loaf_obtain:
The kitchen fills with warmth and the smell of fresh bread.
Feast Loaf obtained.
strings.dialogue.item.flour_sack_pickup:
A heavy cloth sack of flour, still fine and dry.
The pantry kept it perfectly - as if the house wanted a meal made eventually.
strings.dialogue.item.green_pedestal_active:
The Green Pedestal resonates with creative energy and the joy of building.
The Inventor's ingenuity flows through the crystal, sparking new possibilities.
strings.dialogue.item.green_pedestal_active_2: Creative energy spreads through the house like growing vines.
strings.dialogue.item.green_pedestal_inactive:
An emerald pedestal carved with symbols of creation and craftsmanship.
It hums softly, waiting for the Green Crystal Key to awaken its potential.
strings.dialogue.item.hammer_pickup:
A well-used hammer that speaks of creation and honest work.
Carrying it awakens the urge to build and transform.
strings.dialogue.item.hammer_return_place: You return the hammer to its place among the valuables.
strings.dialogue.item.hammer_return_transform: The East Room's creative energy settles back to domestic comfort.
strings.dialogue.item.hammer_transform: The East Room resonates with creative potential.
strings.dialogue.item.jar_of_honey_pickup:
A glass jar of honey, amber and clear.
The label is in handwriting - someone made this themselves, a long time ago.
strings.dialogue.item.journal_page_pickup:
A loose page covered in cramped academic handwriting - footnotes spilling into margins, corrections layered over corrections.
Someone was working something out, and getting closer.
strings.dialogue.item.love_letter_pickup:
A romantic letter filled with promises of eternal love.
Carrying it awakens thoughts of gardens and blooming romance.
strings.dialogue.item.love_letter_return_place: You place the letter back on the nightstand where dreams of love belong.
strings.dialogue.item.love_letter_return_transfo: The North Room's romantic yearning settles back to scholarly calm.
strings.dialogue.item.love_letter_transform: The North Room stirs with romantic longing.
strings.dialogue.item.merchant_ledger_pickup:
A leather-bound ledger, pages dense with transactions.
The last entry is dated December 1943 and cuts off mid-sentence.
strings.dialogue.item.merchant_voucher_pickup:
A letter in a careful hand, signed Augustus Goldstein.
It vouches, briefly and precisely, for the bearer's good character and honest intent.
strings.dialogue.item.ornate_key_pickup:
An ornate key that promises to unlock hidden secrets.
Carrying it awakens thoughts of security and protected treasures.
strings.dialogue.item.ornate_key_return_place: You return the key to its place among the tools and inventions.
strings.dialogue.item.ornate_key_return_transfor: The West Room's protective aura settles back to simple commerce.
strings.dialogue.item.ornate_key_transform: The West Room shifts toward impenetrable security.
strings.dialogue.item.red_pedestal_active:
The Red Pedestal blazes with the light of accumulated knowledge.
The Scholar's wisdom flows through the crystal, illuminating ancient secrets.
strings.dialogue.item.red_pedestal_active_2: Knowledge flows through the house's foundation like rivers of light.
strings.dialogue.item.red_pedestal_inactive:
A crimson pedestal carved with symbols of knowledge and wisdom.
It pulses faintly, waiting for the Red Crystal Key to unlock its power.
strings.dialogue.item.rose_pickup:
A red rose that has not wilted despite everything.
The air around it smells faintly of a garden that should no longer exist.
strings.dialogue.item.safe:
An imposing vault safe covered in mystical symbols.
It emanates an aura of protection and hidden secrets.
strings.dialogue.item.star_chart_pickup:
Ancient astronomical maps covered in mystical calculations.
Carrying it awakens thoughts of celestial observations and cosmic mysteries.
strings.dialogue.item.star_chart_return_place: You return the star chart to its secure place among the other valuable documents.
strings.dialogue.item.star_chart_return_transfor: The South Room's cosmic aspirations settle back to earthly rest.
strings.dialogue.item.star_chart_transform: The South Room reaches toward the stars and cosmic understanding.
strings.dialogue.item.telescope_pickup:
A brass telescope for observing celestial phenomena.
Through its lens, you can see the cosmic patterns that influence earthly events.
strings.dialogue.item.tool_box_pickup:
A weathered box filled with various tools and crafting implements.
Each tool tells a story of problems solved and things built.
strings.dialogue.item.toolbox_assembled_obtain:
The handle slots into the body with a satisfying click.
Tool Box assembled.
strings.dialogue.item.toolbox_body_pickup:
The metal body of a toolbox - dented in a few places, latches still functional.
Apart from the missing handle, it's intact.
strings.dialogue.item.toolbox_handle_pickup:
The wooden handle of a toolbox - solid, worn smooth by decades of use.
It fits the hand perfectly. Someone used this constantly.
strings.dialogue.item.yellow_pedestal_active:
The Yellow Pedestal shimmers with the light of prophetic dreams.
The Dreamer's visions flow through the crystal, revealing glimpses of freedom.
strings.dialogue.item.yellow_pedestal_active_2: Prophetic energy swirls through the house like golden mist.
strings.dialogue.item.yellow_pedestal_inactive:
A golden pedestal carved with symbols of dreams and visions.
It glows softly, waiting for the Yellow Crystal Key to fulfill its destiny.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_ask_cedric:
Cedric is principled, which I respect, even when it's inconvenient.
He confiscated my ledger about forty years ago. He claimed it was for safekeeping.
I maintain it was an overreach. He maintains it was procedure.
We have not reached an agreement on this point.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_ask_help:
It's in Cedric's vault. He won't open it without two conditions — the Ancient Seal secured, and my ledger returned.
I can help you with Cedric if you help me first.
That's how business works, even here.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_ask_vault:
The Blue Crystal Key, among other things.
Also my ledger, which Cedric confiscated on technical grounds I still dispute.
He won't open the vault without two conditions — the Seal secured and the ledger returned.
Which means I need the ledger back before either of us gets what we want.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_complete:
The vault opened, the key is in your hands.
I've been waiting eighty years for someone with enough sense to do this.
I want it noted that I was helpful.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_first_1:
Ah. A visitor who actually looks like they're going somewhere.
Most people in this house have given up moving with any purpose.
[b]Augustus Goldstein[/b]. Merchant. Eighty years in this place and my instincts are still sharp.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_first_2:
I suspect you're here about the Blue Crystal Key.
I know where it is. Whether I help you depends on whether we can do business.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_first_2.choic: What do you know about the Guardian?
I need the Blue Crystal Key.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_has_gold_1:
My coins. Still exactly the right weight.
[i]he counts them without looking down[/i]
Splendid. A deal's a deal.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_has_gold_2:
Here — a letter of introduction. Show it to Cedric alongside the Seal and the Ledger.
I wrote it out years ago on the off chance someone came through here with actual initiative.
The Blue Crystal Key is in that vault. Get it, use it on the blue pedestal in the main hall.
All four pedestals — that's the end of this.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_has_gold_3:
Obtained Merchant Voucher
You now have {keys_collected|round} of 4 Crystal Keys.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_needs_gold:
My gold coins — somewhere in the house.
You have {item_count:item=Gold Coins|bool:them/not found them yet}.
Bring them back and I'll write you the letter for Cedric.
strings.dialogue.merchant.merchant_the_deal:
My gold coins went missing in all of this. They're in the house somewhere — I couldn't tell you exactly where.
Bring them back to me and I'll write you a letter of introduction for Cedric.
He trusts procedure. A voucher from me gives you standing.
That's the deal.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_ask_curse:
Theodore Ashfield — my great-nephew — performed a binding ritual in 1943.
He thought he was preserving the house. He was right, in the most catastrophic sense.
I have been documenting the precise mechanism ever since, so it can be undone.
Which brings me to my current problem.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_ask_elara:
She tends the garden. Has done for — well, as long as I can remember, which is saying something.
[i]he turns back to the shelves rather quickly[/i]
South passage. She'll have her own terms.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_ask_pages:
My journal pages — three of them, the core of my reconstruction work — were scattered when the house last shifted.
North room, east room, west room. Cramped handwriting — you'll recognise them.
Bring all three back and I can read them together. Context is everything.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_complete:
The tome is back. The key is yours.
Four pedestals in the main hall — all four keys together will break the curse.
You have {keys_collected|round} so far. Keep going.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_decoded:
The cabinet key is with Elara — the Gardener, through the south passage.
Tell her Edmund sent you.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_first_1:
Welcome to my library, fellow seeker of knowledge.
I've been here since 1943 — trapped, yes, but the books remained, so the work continued.
I am [b]Edmund Ashfield[/b]. Please, do not knock anything over.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_first_2: Eighty years of research in this room alone. If I could only find my notes...
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_goodbye:
Quite all right. The pages — north room, east room, west room. All three, please.
I'll be here.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_has_pages_1:
All three — yes! That's my hand.
Quick, let me read them together. Context is everything with reconstruction work.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_has_pages_2:
The tome was locked away. Here — 'secured the volume in the oak cabinet, gave the key to...'
[i]a long pause[/i]
...to Elara. For safekeeping.
I see. Well.
Elara tends the garden. She would still have the key — she keeps everything. You should speak to her.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_has_tome_1:
My tome. Good lord, it's exactly as I left it.
[i]he runs a hand across the cover[/i]
Thank you. Genuinely.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_has_tome_2:
The Crystal Key of Knowledge — take it. The red pedestal in the main hall is where it goes.
There are four pedestals in total. You will need all four keys to break the curse.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_has_tome_3:
Obtained Red Crystal Key
You now have {keys_collected|round} of 4 Crystal Keys.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_knows_cabinet:
The Gardener has the cabinet key. I gave it to her some years ago for safekeeping.
She is in the garden — south passage. She will want something in exchange.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_needs_pages:
You have {item_count:item=Journal Page|round} of 3 pages so far.
North room, east room, west room — cramped handwriting, dense margins.
All three before I can read them properly.
strings.dialogue.scholar.scholar_pages_done: Good. South passage to the garden. She will want something in exchange — she always does.
strings.menu.main.title: Memory Palace
strings.menu.settings.title: Settings
